sentences.text: The known teeth of Pliogonodon are conical, curve slightly inward, and are estimated to be around 2 inches long if fully preserved.
These teeth feature wrinkled enamel and hollow bases at the crowns.
The genus Pliogonodon was named by Joseph Leidy in 1856 based on a worn and broken tooth found at Phoebus Landing on the Cape Fear River in North Carolina.
Pliogonodon is classified as an extinct genus of crocodylomorph placed within the parent group Goniopholididae.
The current scientific consensus is that Pliogonodon is a specimen of Deinosuchus.
Pliogonodon fossils are assigned to the Late Cretaceous period, although the original strata age was unrecorded and the holotype is thought to come from Miocene-age beds.
It is debated whether Pliogonodon is synonymous with the alligatoroid Deinosuchus.
